text: "Do not judge, so that you will not be judged.
For with the judgment you use to judge, you will be judged; and with the measure you use to measure, it will be measured to you.
Why do you look at the speck in your brother's eye and pay no attention to the beam in your own?
Or how can you say to your brother, 'Let me take the speck out of your eye,' when all the while there is a beam in your own eye?
You hypocrite! First take the beam out of your own eye, and then you will see clearly enough to take the speck out of your brother's eye.
Do not give what is holy to dogs, and do not throw your pearls in front of pigs. They will only trample them underfoot, then turn and tear you to pieces.
Ask, and it will be given to you; seek, and you will find; knock, and the door will be opened to you.
For everyone who asks receives, and the one who seeks finds, and to the one who knocks the door will be opened.
Which of you, if your son asks you for bread, would hand him a stone?
Or if he asks for a fish, would hand him a snake?
So if you, evil as you are, know how to give good gifts to your children, how much more will your Father in heaven give good things to those who ask him!
So in everything, do to others what you would have them do to you; for this is the Law and the Prophets.
Enter through the narrow gate. For wide is the gate and broad is the road that leads to destruction, and many go through it.
But narrow is the gate and hard is the road that leads to life, and few find it.
Beware of false prophets. They come to you in sheep's clothing, but inwardly they are ravenous wolves.

versions.text: Beware of false prophets. They come to you dressed as sheep, but inwardly they are ravenous wolves.
versions.explanation: The Greek ἐν ἐνδύμασι προβάτων is literally 'in sheep's clothing' — a disguise worn over the wolf. 'Dressed as sheep' weakens the image of a covering garment and loses the familiar, vivid metaphor that reads well aloud.

text: You will recognize them by their fruit. Are grapes gathered from thornbushes, or figs from thistles?
In the same way, every good tree bears good fruit, but a rotten tree bears bad fruit.
A good tree cannot bear bad fruit, and a rotten tree cannot bear good fruit.
Every tree that does not bear good fruit is cut down and thrown into the fire.
So then, you will recognize them by their fruit.
Not everyone who says to me, 'Lord, Lord,' will enter the kingdom of heaven, but the one who does the will of my Father in heaven.
On that day many will say to me, 'Lord, Lord, did we not prophesy in your name, and drive out demons in your name, and perform many miracles in your name?'
Then I will tell them plainly, 'I never knew you. Away from me, you who practice lawlessness.'
Therefore everyone who hears these words of mine and acts on them will be like a wise man who built his house on the rock.

versions.text: Therefore everyone who hears these words of mine and acts on them is like a wise man who built his house on the rock.
versions.explanation: ὁμοιωθήσεται is future passive ('will be likened / will be like'). The present 'is like' loses the future orientation, which points toward the coming judgment described in the surrounding verses.

text: The rain came down, the rivers rose, the winds blew and beat against that house, and it did not fall, because its foundation was on the rock.
But everyone who hears these words of mine and does not act on them will be like a foolish man who built his house on the sand.

versions.text: But everyone who hears these words of mine and does not act on them is like a foolish man who built his house on the sand.
versions.explanation: As in verse 24, the verb is future passive (ὁμοιωθήσεται). Rendering it as future also keeps the two halves of the parable parallel in sound and structure.

text: The rain came down, the rivers rose, the winds blew and struck that house, and it fell with a great crash."
When Jesus had finished saying these words, the crowds were astounded at his teaching,

versions.text: When Jesus had finished saying all this, the crowds were astounded at his teaching,
versions.explanation: τοὺς λόγους τούτους is 'these words/sayings'; 'all this' generalizes and adds 'all', which is not in the Greek. 'These words' also echoes the wording of verses 24 and 26, tying the closing formula back to the parable.

text: because he taught them as one who had authority, and not as their scribes.
